Routing mode: pre-FY (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). Interpreting incoming RNS as FY results accordingly. Next year end = 31/12/25 → FY1 = FY25 · prior year = FY24 · FY2 = FY26. Sharescope data reflects the pre-RNS state.

Year label mappings (derived from Next year end = 31/12/25):

  • FY1 = FY25 (1y fc in Sharescope)
  • FY1−1 = FY24 (1y ago in Sharescope)
  • FY1−2 = FY23 (2y ago in Sharescope)
  • FY1−3 = FY22 (3y ago in Sharescope)
  • FY2 = FY26 (2y fc in Sharescope)

PHASE 1 — DATA CONTEXT

JTC · Q2 · Full Year Results · FY25 · Year end: 31/12/25

  • Routing: pre-FY mode (Q2). Incoming RNS = FY25 full year results.
  • FY1 consensus (FY25e): EPS 49.7p · Revenue £385.1m
  • FY2 consensus (FY26e): EPS 60.4p · Revenue £454.8m
  • Forecast broker momentum: EPS net change −0.2p (−0.2%) over full snapshot period. Last-4-week trend: 🟡 STALLING (flat at 49.7p since 13 Mar 26). Revenue net change: £385.1m vs £387.3m at earliest snapshot = −£2.2m (−0.6%). No net upgrades visible in the snapshot window — consensus has drifted marginally lower.
  • H1 baselines (3yr avg): Revenue 47.3% of FY = £182.2m · EPS 46.5% of FY = 23.1p
  • Prior-year H1 actuals (FY24): Revenue £147.1m · EPS 19.9p
  • Implied H2 YoY (pre-FY mode, RNS-derived): FY25 actual £381.9m − H1 actual £172.6m = implied H2 Rev £209.3m vs prior H2 £158.3m → +32.2% YoY. FY25 EPS 45.55p − H1 actual 21.3p = implied H2 EPS 24.25p vs prior H2 27.5p → −11.8% YoY.
  • FX: Revenue growth on constant currency basis 26.7% vs reported 25.1% — difference = 1.6pp, exceeding 0.5pp threshold. USD is material exposure (~32% of revenue). Phase 0B triggered — assessed below.
  • Reporting currency & debt: GBP · Net debt (underlying): FY23 £13.9m → FY24 £182.3m → FY25 £275.8m (actual) → FY26fc £232.3m · ND/EBITDA: FY23 3.2x / FY24 1.9x (underlying) / FY25 2.22x (actual) / FY26fc 1.6x · Interest cover FY25 actual: 0.9x (reported) / 3.9x (fc — note fc was pre-RNS) · ND/FCF FY25fc: 3.4x · Debt flag: 🟡 Manageable leverage — 2.22x underlying EBITDA, above 1.5–2.0x guidance but anticipated; annualised acquisitions bring within range. Interest cover on underlying basis adequate; reported cover distorted by EIP/non-underlying items.

Phase 0B assessment: USD ~32% of revenue. Constant currency growth 26.7% vs reported 25.1% = 1.6pp difference — GBP strengthening created a headwind. 1.6pp exceeds 0.5pp threshold so override does not fire. However, exposure is 30–35% band and impact is modest (1.6pp on revenue). Applying mid-point of 30–35% headwind band: 🔴 GBP headwind — FX Rule 1 applied (−4 pts mid-point of −4 band for modest headwind). Badge: FX Rule 1 applied (−4 pts) · ~32% USD · GBP headwind.

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

JTC · Q2 · Full Year Results · FY25 · Year end: 31/12/25

RNS type: Full Year Results

1. Revenue — FY25 actual FY25 revenue: £381.9m (+25.1% YoY vs FY24 £305.4m). Vs FY25e consensus £385.1m = miss of £3.2m (−0.8%). Inorganic contributed £55.1m (Citi Trust, KHT). Organic growth 8.5% (vs 11.3% in FY24). Constant currency growth 26.7%.

"Revenue grew 25.1% to £381.9m (2024: £305.4m) and underlying EBITDA increased 22.4% to £124.5m (2024: £101.7m). Net organic growth was 8.5% (2024: 11.3%)."

Implied H2 revenue: £381.9m − £172.6m = £209.3m vs prior H2 £158.3m (+32.2% YoY) — strong, driven by Citi Trust H2 contribution (acquired 1 Jul 2025, contributed £32.8m inorganic in period).

2. EPS / earnings — FY25 actual Underlying basic EPS: 45.55p (+9.0% YoY vs FY24 41.80p). Vs FY25e consensus 49.7p = miss of 4.15p (−8.3%). Reported basic EPS 0.56p (2024: −4.44p). The EPS miss vs consensus is material.

"Underlying basic EPS (a / b): 45.55p (2024: 41.80p). The growth in underlying EPS of 9.0% was relatively lower than EBITDA growth of 22.4%. This was driven by the increased interest expense on our borrowings that fund M&A activity (with only a 6 month contribution from Citi and 2 months from KHT), and the increased volume of shares in the period."

EPS quality check: Effective tax rate on underlying profit = £7.4m tax on £8.4m PBT (reported) = 88.8% — but this is heavily distorted by non-underlying items. On underlying basis: tax charge not separately broken out cleanly, but the CFO notes effective tax rate 5.8% on underlying basis (2024: 4.9%). 5.8% is low but consistent with Jersey domicile. No material deviation from prior year normalised rate. No tax-distorted beat — the miss is genuine. 🚨 Note: acquisition dilution (interest step-up from £184.2m drawdowns, share count increase from Galaxy EIP award exercise) compressed the EPS bridge materially.

FY26e EPS bridge (constructed here, referenced in Phase 4 #2):

  • New base: FY25 underlying EPS 45.55p (168.0m shares)
  • Inorganic annualisation delta: Citi Trust contributed 6 months (H2 only) in FY25 — full annualisation in FY26 adds ~£32.8m × 2 − £32.8m = +£32.8m incremental revenue; at 32.6% EBITDA margin = ~+£10.7m EBITDA. KHT contributed 2 months — full year adds ~£14.5m revenue at ~37% margin = ~+£5.4m EBITDA. Combined annualisation EBITDA uplift ~£16.1m.
  • Organic EBITDA growth delta: disclosed organic growth 8.5% — applying to FY25 organic revenue base ~£321m × 8.5% × 32.6% margin ≈ +£8.9m EBITDA organic contribution.
  • Interest step-up delta: FY25 bank loan interest £21.6m on average drawn debt. FY26 will see full-year cost of £184.2m net drawdowns at SONIA+ margin + US PP notes at 6.25%. Estimated FY26 interest: ~£28–30m (vs FY25 £21.6m) = incremental ~£6–8m interest headwind vs FY25 actuals.
  • Net EBITDA uplift (annualisation + organic): ~+£25m; minus additional D&A on acquired intangibles (~£5m uplift from full-year Citi/KHT); minus interest step-up ~£7m; minus tax at ~7% effective = net underlying profit uplift ~£11–13m.
  • Implied FY26 underlying profit: £76.5m + £11–13m = ~£87.5–89.5m. At 168m shares = ~52–53p EPS.
  • Stale FY26 consensus: 60.4p. Implied shortfall vs consensus: −7.4 to −8.4p (−12 to −14%).
  • This strongly suggests FY26 consensus needs to come down. The stale consensus appears to have assumed either higher organic growth or lower interest costs than actuals now imply.

3. Order book / forward work New business wins record: £43.5m (+21.8% vs FY24 £35.7m). Revenue retention 98.6% (FY24: 98.4%). Pipeline described as "healthy". No specific order book figure disclosed.

"We had another record year of new business wins totalling £43.5m at the period end (2024: £35.7m). The new business pipeline remains healthy."

4. Margin, profitability, costs Underlying EBITDA: £124.5m (+22.4% YoY). Underlying EBITDA margin 32.6% (FY24: 33.3%) — down 0.7pp. Management's medium-term guidance range: 33–38%. FY25 margin is below the bottom of the guidance range. ICS margin 28.8% (FY24: 30.6%) — deterioration flagged as investment-driven plus regulatory headwind on chargeable time. PCS margin 37.3% (FY24: 37.3%) — flat, showing Citi Trust integration delivered at JTC margins. Finance costs up 34.0% YoY (£31.2m vs £25.4m), driven by £184.2m debt drawdowns.

"Our underlying EBITDA margin reported a drop to 32.6% (2024: 33.3%). 2025 continued to be a year of market volatility, with the impact being most prominent in the ICS division."

Forward-looking margin guidance: nil explicit numeric. Management commentary references continued investment in infrastructure and regulatory compliance. No guidance for FY26 margin improvement stated.

5. Capital returns and balance sheet Dividend: 5p total for FY25 (FY24: 12.54p). Cut of 60.1% — driven entirely by the pending Permira acquisition. No final dividend declared due to offer period. This is a one-off structural event, not a going-concern signal.

Net debt (underlying) at FY25 year-end: £275.8m (vs FY24: £182.3m). Underlying ND/EBITDA: 2.22x (vs guidance 1.5–2.0x, above range as expected post-M&A). Undrawn facilities: £27.4m of £400m bank + $100m of $175m US PP.

"Our underlying net debt/underlying EBITDA leverage at the period end was 2.22x (2024: 1.79x), above our guidance range (1.5x - 2.0x). This increase was expected, with the period seeing increased M&A activity."

6. Qualitative tone / acquisition context Permira acquisition: agreed at £13.40/share (Nov 2025). Shareholder approval received Jan 2026. Expected to complete Q3 2026. This is the dominant structural overlay — the company is in an offer period, no earnings guidance can be given, no broker presentations held.

"Based on current expectations, the transaction is expected to complete during the third quarter of 2026, subject to satisfaction of the remaining conditions."

7. Constant currency / FX Constant currency revenue growth 26.7% vs reported 25.1% — 1.6pp drag from GBP strengthening vs USD.

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification

JTC is in an active offer period (Permira £13.40 cash bid). No FY26 guidance is given — legally restricted from doing so. The RNS closes the Cosmos era and introduces "Genesis" under private ownership. No earnings trajectory stated for FY26. No "comfortable with" language. No "ahead of expectations" language.

Classification: 🟡 In-line for outlook — but this is structurally constrained by the offer period. There is no positive upgrade signal and no downgrade warning beyond the mechanical miss on FY25 EPS vs consensus.

Exact guidance phrase: none — offer period restriction. Guidance: nil (qualitative only — "resilient", "record wins", "healthy pipeline"). Covers: not applicable. Provisional points: 0 to +3 (In-line, upper end given record new wins and healthy pipeline language, but nil numeric guidance caps this).

Divergence check: FY25 EPS missed consensus by 8.3%, yet qualitative language is constructive ("resilient performance", "record new business wins"). Current year miss + constructive qualitative tone = divergence. Carry as: 🟡 Beat quality — forward guidance diverges from current year delivery (EPS missed consensus materially; qualitative tone does not reflect this adequately).

3.4 Forecast Broker Momentum Overlay

3.5 Balance Sheet & Debt Profile

  • ND/FCF: FY25fc 3.4x / FY26fc 2.4x

Debt flag: 🟡 Manageable leverage — 2.22x ND/EBITDA, above 1.5–2.0x guidance but explicitly anticipated and expected to revert to range when annualising acquisitions. Interest cover adequate. Covenant risk low given undrawn facilities. No Phase 5 scored row.

Forecast year earnings check:

Step 1 — FY25 vs FY24 actual:

  • FY25 actual EPS 45.55p vs FY24 actual 41.80p → ✅ growing (+9.0%)
  • FY25 actual Revenue £381.9m vs FY24 actual £305.4m → ✅ growing (+25.1%)
  • ✅✅ FY25 EPS and Revenue both growing vs prior year actual.

Step 2 — FY26 fc vs FY25 actual:

  • FY26fc EPS 60.4p vs FY25 actual 45.55p → ✅ growing (+32.6%) — but EPS bridge implies 60.4p is materially overstated; realistic FY26 EPS ~52–53p.
  • FY26fc Revenue £454.8m vs FY25 actual £381.9m → ✅ growing (+19.1%)
  • ✅✅ FY26fc EPS and Revenue both growing vs FY25 actual on stale consensus. However: 🚨 FY26 consensus EPS 60.4p likely overstated by ~8–10p vs implied bridge (~52–53p) — stale consensus pre-acquisition annualisation maths and pre-interest-step-up.

3.6 Structural flags

Permira acquisition overlay: JTC is subject to a recommended cash offer at £13.40/share. Expected Q3 2026 completion. This makes FY26 broker forecasts largely irrelevant for investment purposes — the instrument will be delisted. Any broker revisions post-RNS are mechanical exercises only. The offer price is the terminal value.

"Based on current expectations, the transaction is expected to complete during the third quarter of 2026, subject to satisfaction of the remaining conditions."

Organic growth deceleration: 8.5% (FY25) vs 11.3% (FY24) — rolling 3yr avg 13.2%. Management acknowledges macro headwinds (fund launch delays, interest rate headwind to Banking/Treasury services). Medium-term guidance 10%+ — FY25 is below this.

"The subdued organic growth for the year was a result of macroeconomic conditions, albeit strong in the context of our overall market."

PHASE 4 — BROKER-REACTION SIMULATION

JTC · Q2 · Full Year Results · FY25 · Year end: 31/12/25

#1 Driver — EPS miss vs consensus The dominant #1 driver is the EPS shortfall of 4.15p (−8.3%) vs FY25e consensus of 49.7p. Underlying EPS 45.55p is below the entire consensus range. Interest step-up from £184.2m net drawdowns and partial acquisition contribution are the mechanical causes. Brokers will need to cut FY25 actuals through their models and reassess FY26 from this lower base. This is the single metric that drives all revision activity.

#2 Driver — FY26 EPS consensus reset The #2 driver is the implied FY26 consensus reset. Stale consensus at 60.4p was built on assumptions that pre-dated the Citi Trust acquisition's full P&L impact (higher interest, partial EBITDA). The EPS bridge (Phase 2) implies ~52–53p as the realistic FY26 level — a ~−12 to −14% cut required. Revenue consensus (£454.8m) is more defensible given annualisation of Citi/KHT, but EPS leverage is the crux.

#2 Forecast revisions (FY25 and FY26):

  • FY25 EPS: actual 45.55p vs 49.7p consensus — no revision needed, actuals published. Models reset to 45.55p base.
  • FY26 EPS: expected revision down to ~52–53p from 60.4p = approximately −12 to −14%. Direction: cut.
  • FY25 Revenue: actual £381.9m vs £385.1m consensus = −0.8% miss. Minor.
  • FY26 Revenue: likely modest cut from £454.8m toward ~£440–450m reflecting lower organic growth trajectory and FX headwind. Direction: modest cut, −1 to −3%.
  • FY26 EPS revision direction: cut. Net FY1 (now FY26) EPS revision: cut.

#3 Target price and recommendation: Consensus TP is £13.00 — irrelevant. The Permira offer at £13.40 is the effective ceiling and floor for the share price. Brokers will formally mark TPs to the offer price (£13.40) or close to it. Recommendations will shift to "accept offer" / tender. No traditional upgrade/downgrade dynamic applies. Current price £13.04 implies a 2.8% discount to offer — spread reflects regulatory completion risk (Q3 2026).

#4 Conservative guidance read-through: No guidance language at all — offer period restriction. No "not less than" language. No "comfortable with" language. There is no upgrade cycle probability — the company is being acquired. This is the terminal RNS.

#5 Key risk: The single largest risk is regulatory delay or deal failure. If Permira's acquisition does not complete (regulatory rejection, competing bid, JTC break-up), the share would reprice sharply lower toward fundamental value — which on a 45.55p EPS base and pre-offer multiple would be well below £13.40. Additionally, ongoing organic growth deceleration (8.5% vs 10%+ target) and ICS margin compression (28.8% vs 30.6%) represent structural concerns if the deal were to fall away.

"All necessary regulatory consents and required completion approvals are now being sought and the process continues to move forward positively."

Consistency check: Net FY26 EPS revision direction = cut (−12 to −14%). Tone must be: Cautious or Negative. However, the deal context overrides: brokers are not issuing traditional revision notes — they are issuing "accept offer" notes. The mechanical revision exercise (EPS cut) would be classified Cautious, but the deal context means no active downgrade cycle fires in the conventional sense.

On fundamentals alone, at 45.55p EPS and a historically appropriate trust/professional services multiple of 20–25x, intrinsic value would be £9–11, well below the £13.04 current price — the premium is entirely deal-dependent. 🏁 Score 38/100: Cautious — the FY25 RNS delivers a material EPS miss of 8.3% and implies a FY26 consensus reset of −12 to −14%; deal context caps downside but underlying revision dynamics are firmly negative.

Routing mode: pre-FY (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). Interpreting incoming RNS as FY results accordingly. Next year end = 31/12/25 → FY1 = FY25 · prior year = FY24 · FY2 = FY26. Sharescope data reflects the pre-RNS state.

PHASE 1 — DATA CONTEXT

KOO · Q2 · Full Year Results · FY25 · Year end: 31/12/25

  • Routing: pre-FY mode (Q2). Incoming RNS is Full Year Results for FY25. Market now shifts focus to FY26 guidance.
  • FY1 consensus (FY25e — now actuals): EPS 9.0p · Revenue £63.3m
  • FY2 consensus (FY26e): EPS 9.4p · Revenue £63.1m
  • Forecast broker momentum: EPS started 9.0p in May 2025, drifted down to 8.3p by September 2025 (−8.3%), recovered to 9.4p in late January 2026 (+13.3%), then fell back to 9.0p at 28 March → 02 April. Net change over full period: 0.0%. Last 4 weeks: 🔴 FALLING (9.4p → 9.0p over 4 weeks, −0.44p). Revenue: £66.6m → £63.3m (−4.9% net). The revenue consensus has converged to exactly the FY25 actual — strongly suggesting the actual was pre-released or the guidance set this level. EPS sequence: down then up then down again = unstable consensus reflecting uncertainty about FX, Michigan timing.
  • H1 baselines (3yr avg): Revenue 42.8% of FY = £27.1m · EPS: only 1yr avg available (47.6% of FY) = 4.3p
  • Prior-year H1 actuals (FY24): Revenue £32.5m · EPS 10.0p

Note: Sharescope shows FY1 fc EPS at 9.0p and current H1 EPS at −3.0p. This is a critical flag — the H1 was deeply loss-making while the full-year was expected to be 9.0p profit. The H2 was therefore bearing the entire earnings burden: FY1 fc 9.0p − H1 actual −3.0p = H2 burden 12.0p. This is an extraordinary H2 burden and the key analytical challenge for KOO.

  • Implied H2 YoY: Revenue: FY1 fc £63.3m − H1 actual £32.1m = implied H2 £31.2m vs FY24 H2 £34.3m → −9.1% YoY. EPS: FY1 fc 9.0p − H1 actual −3.0p = implied H2 12.0p vs FY24 H2 11.0p → +9.1% YoY.
  • FX: 74% of revenues in USD per RNS. Material — Phase 0B will trigger.
  • Reporting currency & debt: GBP · Net cash (negative borrowings): FY23 −£0.1m (net cash £0.1m) / FY24 −£6.9m (net cash £6.9m) / H1 FY25 −£15.3m → FY1fc −£21.6m (net cash) / FY2fc −£25.4m · ND/EBITDA all negative (net cash position) · Interest cover: N/A (no debt) · Debt flag: 🟢 Unlevered / net cash — £21.6m cash, zero debt, $9.5m undrawn facility.

PHASE 0B — FX REVENUE CHECK

74% of revenues in USD. This exceeds the 50%+ threshold materially.

Searched the web

GBP/USD spot: ~$1.32 today. KOO's RNS discloses prior year FY25 average rate implicitly — CFO review states GBP appreciation against USD drove £3.3m FX headwind on ARR. The RNS explicitly states "approximately 74% of revenues and 50% of expenses denominated in US Dollars" and "realised foreign currency loss of £0.6m." The CFO confirms the FX impact: the 2025 GBP/USD average was materially stronger than 2024. From the RNS, a 10% rate change = £1.4m profit impact, implying a roughly $1.27–1.29 average in 2024 and $1.30–1.32 average in 2025 (consistent with search data: 2026 YTD average ~$1.35).

KOO Phase 0B:

  • USD exposure: 74% of revenues (>50% threshold)
  • Spot rate today: ~$1.32
  • Prior year (FY25) average from RNS context: ~$1.28–1.30 (consistent with reported FX loss of £0.6m on £46.1m US revenues)
  • FY24 average: ~$1.27 per CFO disclosures

For FY26 guidance purposes: spot $1.32 vs FY25 avg ~$1.29 → GBP slightly stronger. Modest ongoing headwind for FY26 but less severe than FY25's drag.

For FY25 actuals (the current RNS): the FX headwind is already baked into the reported numbers — £63.3m actual revenue includes the drag. The Phase 0B penalty for FY25 actuals is therefore already in the numbers and should not be double-counted. For FY26 forward guidance context, the spot is ~$1.32 vs FY25 avg ~$1.29 — neutral to marginal headwind.

Phase 0B for KOO FY25 results: FX headwind already reflected in actuals. The RNS explicitly quantifies: constant currency revenue −2.7% vs reported −5.1% → FX impact = ~2.4pp on revenues. For the Phase 5 scoring, the FX damage is already in the delivered numbers, so I will NOT apply a fresh Phase 0B penalty to the score (the actual result already incorporates it). However, I will flag FX as a structural risk for FY26 forward estimates.

Badge: For FY26 forward risk: FX headwind ongoing · 74% USD · $1.32 spot vs ~$1.29 FY25 avg · modest continued drag on FY26

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

KOO · Q2 · Full Year Results · FY25 · Year end: 31/12/25

RNS type: Full Year Results

1. Revenue FY25 actual revenue: £63.3m vs FY24 £66.7m = −5.1% YoY. vs FY1 pre-RNS consensus £63.3m = in line (consensus had already converged to the actual — the weekly Sharescope data shows consensus moving to exactly £63.3m on 30 January 2026, suggesting a pre-announcement briefing or interim guidance). Constant currency: −2.7%. ARR: £60.6m (2024: £66.4m), −8.7% reported, −3.7% constant currency.

"2025 revenue was £63.3m (2024: £66.7m), following a record year in 2024 in which revenues doubled. This figure reflects the impact of FX movements, a reduction in California product development revenues and delays in signing a contract with the State of Michigan."

H2 implied: £63.3m − £32.1m H1 = £31.2m vs FY24 H2 £34.3m = −9.0% YoY. Revenue was back-end light, consistent with Michigan contract revenue pushed to FY26.

2. EPS / Earnings Reported basic EPS: 7p (£0.07 per share). Diluted: 7p. Per Sharescope FY1 fc EPS 9.0p (adjusted basis).

From P&L: PBT £4.37m → tax £1.76m → PAT £2.61m. Diluted shares: 38.6m. Diluted reported EPS = 6.8p (£2.608m / 38.557m). The 9.0p FY1 Sharescope consensus is on an adjusted basis — need to derive.

Adjusted EBITDA: £11.3m (consensus "ahead of expectations" — this is the one explicit beat). Adj EBITDA FY24: £15.8m → FY25: £11.3m = −28.5%.

EPS quality check — CRITICAL: The CFO explicitly flags an effective tax rate of 40.3% vs standard rate of 25%. Two permanent differences cited:

  1. Transition from SME R&D to RDEC scheme: R&D now in "other income" (£0.3m) rather than as a tax credit. Prior year had £0.5m in tax credits.
  2. Share-based payment permanent difference: SBP charges not deductible on vesting where share price fell below grant price — caused ~10pp of ETR increase.

These are structural/accounting changes, not true earnings distortions in the trading sense. The RDEC reclassification is revenue-side neutral (£0.3m in "other income"). The SBP non-deductibility is a genuine non-recurring tax drag.

Restated at normalised 25% tax rate: PBT £4.37m × 75% = £3.28m PAT. Diluted EPS restated = £3.28m / 38.6m = 8.5p. The reported 6.8p includes ~1.7p of abnormal tax drag. This matters for assessing whether FY25 is a clean base for FY26. However — the RDEC/SBP issues may partly recur in FY26, so I will note the distortion but use the reported figure as the baseline.

🚨 EPS quality flag: Effective tax rate 40.3% vs normalised 25% — 15.3pp above standard rate. Restated adj EPS at 25% = ~8.5p vs reported ~6.8p. The £0.6m SBP non-deductibility and RDEC reclassification account for most of the gap. This is partly recurring (if SBP awards vest below grant, the permanent difference continues in FY26) and partly non-recurring (RDEC reclassification is now the new base). FY26 ETR should normalise towards ~30–32% as RDEC effect stabilises.

FY26e EPS bridge:

  • FY25 base: adj EBITDA £11.3m; D&A £6.2m; adj EBIT ~£5.1m; interest income £0.7m (cash deposits on £21.6m); PBT ~£4.4m (consistent with reported); at normalised 30% tax → PAT ~£3.1m; diluted EPS ~8.0p
  • (1) New base: ~8.0p on clean tax
  • (2) Revenue guidance FY26: "in line with current market expectations" — FY2 consensus £63.1m = essentially flat. No revenue growth assumption.
  • (3) Michigan contract: £2.6m signed post-period. This was delayed from FY25 — will now recognise in FY26. Net new FY26 revenue vs FY25: +£2.6m (partially offset by any California reductions). ARR at year-end £60.6m but contract backlog (revenue to come) £22.8m → all recognised within one year. Strong FY26 revenue floor from contracted backlog.
  • (4) California direct marketing: £8.1m in FY25 (vs £3.9m FY24). This is a "front-loaded" investment. The RNS implies this investment level does not need to repeat at the same intensity once users are registered. If direct marketing reduces to £4–5m in FY26, gross margin improves ~£3–4m → adj EBITDA improves materially.
  • (5) UK Soluna launch H2 2026: additional capex/opex ahead of revenue — dilutive short-term.
  • Implied FY26 EPS: £63.1m revenue × improving gross margin (~75–76% if marketing reduces) → gross profit ~£47–48m; opex broadly flat; adj EBITDA ~£12.5–13.5m; D&A ~£6.5m (capex slightly higher for Soluna UK); adj EBIT ~£6.0–7.0m; + interest income ~£0.8m; PBT ~£6.8–7.8m; at 30% tax → PAT ~£4.8–5.5m; diluted EPS ~12–14p at 36–38m diluted shares.

Wait — this is materially above the FY2 consensus of 9.4p. The FY2 consensus may be too conservative if marketing costs normalise. Alternatively, the consensus may be factoring in Soluna UK launch costs + continued California investment at elevated levels. The 9.4p consensus is likely the more realistic base given management's "in line with expectations" language is backward-looking on current consensus. I will flag this as a potential consensus upgrade scenario but not build upside into the base case.

3. Order book / forward visibility Revenue to come from contracts with unfulfilled obligations: £22.8m at 31 December 2025 (2024: £27.1m), all expected within one year. Michigan contract ($2.6m = ~£2.0m) signed post-period — not in this figure. US revenue 71% of total in 2025, with one customer (California) at 71% of Group revenue.

"Revenue to come from contracts entered into with performance obligations not fulfilled or only partially fulfilled amounted to £22.8m as at 31 December 2025 (2024: £27.1m), all of which is expected to be recognised within one year."

4. Margin / profitability Gross margin: 73.1% (FY24: 77.9%), −480bps. The decline is entirely attributable to £8.1m of California direct marketing in cost of sales (vs £3.9m FY24). Excluding the marketing investment: gross margin approximately 86% of revenues ex-marketing = ~80%+.

Adjusted EBITDA: £11.3m — stated "ahead of expectations." This is the only explicit beat in the RNS.

Operating profit: £3.4m (FY24: £9.2m). Admin expenses flat at £42.9m (−£0.1m YoY) showing discipline.

Free cash flow: net inflow £1.2m (FY24: £10.2m). Cash at year-end: £21.6m (FY24: £21.8m) — essentially flat, down only £0.2m despite heavy investment year.

5. Capital returns No dividend (policy: invest for growth). £1.5m share buyback completed in February 2025. No new buyback announced.

6. Qualitative tone — FY26 outlook CEO: "we anticipate that revenue and adjusted EBITDA for 2026 will be in line with current market expectations."

FY2 consensus: Revenue £63.1m, adj EBITDA (from Sharescope) £10.3m. So FY26 guided at flat-to-marginally-down EBITDA (£11.3m → £10.3m) and flat revenue (£63.3m → £63.1m). This is not a positive guide.

Key initiatives: Michigan contract now signed, New Jersey renewed, Soluna UK H2 2026 launch, AI product development, Kismet acquisition (paediatric platform, acquired for $1). No numeric uplift provided on any of these.

7. Post-period events Michigan contract: $2.6m (£~2.0m). This is incremental to FY25 revenue base.

EPS quality check summary: 🚨 ETR 40.3% vs 25% standard rate — 15.3pp gap. Two permanent items: SBP non-deductibility (~10pp) and RDEC reclassification (~5pp). Restated at 30% normalised FY26 rate → FY25 base EPS ~8.0–8.5p. FY26 consensus at 9.4p is plausible if: (a) revenue flat, (b) California marketing normalises somewhat, (c) ETR normalises to 30–32%. But the in-line guidance suggests management is not signalling a beat.

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification

Forward language on FY26: "revenue and adjusted EBITDA for 2026 will be in line with current market expectations." Numeric coverage: qualitative-only, references current consensus. No uplift language. FY2 consensus EBITDA £10.3m is slightly below FY25 actual £11.3m — suggesting management is guiding to a Soluna UK launch cost drag. Revenue flat.

3.6 Structural Flags

California concentration risk: One customer accounts for 71% of Group revenue (£44.9m). Any adverse change to the California contract — political (state budget, governor priorities), contractual (termination for convenience clause exists per accounting policy), or performance-related — would be catastrophic for the business. The RNS provides strong mitigation: LA County motion directing all youth-serving departments to integrate Soluna, joint letter from CalHHS/DHCS/DOE, Northwestern University independent evaluation. But the concentration remains extreme.

"The group had one customer (2024: one) that accounted for more than 10% of total revenue in 2025. This customer accounted for 71% of group revenue (2024: 73%)"

Revenue backlog structure: Contracts include termination-for-convenience clauses with fixed notice periods (IFRS 15 note). This means the £22.8m contract backlog has a shorter "firm" duration than it appears — revenue is recognised monthly but contracts can be exited on notice. Risk asymmetry.

PHASE 4 — BROKER REACTION SIMULATION

KOO · Q2 · Full Year Results · FY25 · Year end: 31/12/25

#1 Driver — Adj EBITDA beat and cash preservation: The only explicit financial beat in the RNS is adj EBITDA of £11.3m "ahead of expectations." Combined with year-end cash of £21.6m (essentially flat vs FY24's £21.8m despite heavy investment and £1.5m buyback) — this is the primary positive. Brokers will note that the investment year did not burn cash as feared, and EBITDA came in ahead. This provides confidence that FY26 EBITDA guidance of ~£10.3m (in-line) is achievable without major cash deterioration. Driver #1.

#2 Driver — California KPI beats and institutional embedding: 144,000+ youth registered on Soluna (exceeding performance targets), LA County directive, Northwestern University evaluation showing "significant and sustained improvements in wellbeing." These are the long-term valuation drivers — they demonstrate Soluna is becoming infrastructure rather than a pilot. The New Jersey renewal and Michigan contract ($2.6m) show the State Alliance model is generating repeat/expansion business. Brokers will use these KPIs to anchor their long-term DCF models (the TP of 314p implies a very long-term value creation thesis). Driver #2 for the investment case narrative.

#2 Forecast revisions — FY25 (FY1) and FY26 (FY2):

FY25 actuals vs consensus:

  • Revenue: £63.3m vs £63.3m consensus = in-line — no revision needed (consensus had pre-converged)
  • Adj EBITDA: £11.3m vs expectations = beat — brokers may upgrade FY25 EBITDA estimate upwards (if not already reflecting the in-line consensus)
  • Reported EPS: 6.8p vs Sharescope 9.0p consensus — significant miss on reported basis due to 40.3% ETR. Brokers using adj basis: adj EBITDA beat suggests adj EPS also beats adj consensus; but reported EPS is the headline that investors see.

FY26 (FY2):

  • Revenue: "in line with current market expectations" = £63.1m held → no change
  • Adj EBITDA: "in line" = ~£10.3m held → hold to modest trim (FY25 £11.3m → FY26 £10.3m already embedded; Soluna UK launch costs could pressure further)
  • EPS: reported EPS base is 6.8p; ETR normalising to ~30–32% in FY26 → FY26 adj EPS ~9.4p consensus achievable. Hold or marginal trim — no upgrade catalyst.

#3 Target price and recommendation: TPs will be held or marginally trimmed. The 314p consensus TP is a long-term DCF value — brokers are unlikely to cut it based on one in-line year. However, the share at 107p vs 314p TP (193% upside) reflects the market's fundamental distrust of that long-term thesis being delivered. Brokers will maintain Buy/Add but acknowledge the near-term uncertainty. No TP cuts expected, no increases expected. Hold TPs at 300–320p range.

#4 Conservative guidance read-through: "In line with current market expectations" is explicitly neutral — not "comfortable with" (constructive) and not a beat flag. No conservative guidance premium. However, management has consistently underpromised and overdelivered on the EBITDA line (FY25 EBITDA beat); brokers may attribute a modest probability of FY26 EBITDA upside if California marketing continues to normalise.

#5 Key risk: California contract termination clause and concentration risk. 71% single-customer revenue with a termination-for-convenience clause is the dominant risk. The geopolitical/budget environment in California (state budgets under pressure, new administration priorities) creates uncertainty. Any California contract reduction or non-renewal would be a company-defining event.

"Revenue to come from contracts entered into with performance obligations not fulfilled or only partially fulfilled amounted to £22.8m as at 31 December 2025 (2024: £27.1m), all of which is expected to be recognised within one year."

Consistency check: Net FY1 (FY25 actuals) outcome vs FY2 (FY26) revision direction = hold. Revenue in-line, EBITDA beat is FY25 not FY26. FY26 guided in-line. Tone = Neutral. ✅ Consistent.

EBITDA beat and California KPI beats provide near-term comfort but: revenue flat, FY26 guided in-line at lower EBITDA, reported EPS significantly below adjusted expectations (tax distortion), extreme single-customer concentration. Brokers will maintain recommendations but not initiate upgrades.

Raw score: 42

Para 1 — Headline numbers: KOO delivered FY25 results that are best characterised as "broadly held together." Revenue of £63.3m (consensus exactly) and adj EBITDA of £11.3m "ahead of expectations" are the two headline figures — the EBITDA beat is the singular positive. The problem is what sits beneath: reported EPS of 6.8p (diluted) against a Sharescope adj consensus of 9.0p is a significant gap, driven by a 40.3% effective tax rate (vs 25% standard) caused by SBP non-deductibility (share price fell below grant price, ~10pp ETR impact) and the RDEC reclassification (~5pp). The FX headwind of ~£3.3m on ARR is already embedded. The #1 number that dominates is that one customer (California) accounts for 71% of Group revenue — the entire investment case rests on that contract deepening and diversifying.

Para 2 — H2 momentum and upgrade resilience: In pre-FY mode, H2 momentum is the key signal. KOO's implied H2 revenue was £31.2m — down 9.0% YoY vs FY24 H2's £34.3m. The decline is explained: £2m lower California development revenues, Michigan contract (~£2m equivalent) delayed to FY26, and ~£1.5m FX impact in H2. The H2 EPS implied was 9.8p (reported basis) — down 10.9% vs FY24 H2's 11.0p. Both metrics classify as 🔴 weak. The upgrade resilience is entirely structural rather than numerical: the 144,000+ California users, LA County integration directive, and Northwestern evaluation provide the qualitative floor under the investment case — but they do not directly translate into near-term EPS upgrades. FY26 guidance of "in line" with consensus revenue (£63.1m, effectively flat) and lower consensus EBITDA (£10.3m) means H2 momentum carries through to FY26 as well. The Michigan contract ($2.6m) provides a known incremental, partially offsetting the California development revenue reduction.

Para 3 — Broker revisions and verdict: Brokers will make minimal revisions. FY25 actuals are in-line on revenue (pre-converged consensus), slightly ahead on EBITDA — no meaningful FY25 number changes needed. For FY26: revenue held at £63.1m, EBITDA held at ~£10.3m (possibly trimmed marginally given Soluna UK launch costs), reported EPS towards 9–10p if the ETR normalises towards 30–32% (the SBP permanent difference will reduce if KOO shares recover). TP range 300–320p held, but the 107p share price vs 314p TP represents a credibility gap that today's RNS does not close — the market needs to see FY26 revenue growth and California contract durability evidenced. The single watch point is the California contract — a £22.8m contracted backlog covering only ~36% of FY26 revenue guidance means ~64% of FY26 revenue depends on contracts being renewed/extended over the course of the year. 🏁 Hold and wait: EBITDA beat is noted but insufficient to re-rate; FY26 "in-line" guidance removes upgrade catalyst; recovery hinges on Michigan ramp, Soluna UK launch, and California contract durability — none of which crystallise until H2 FY26.

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

RNS type: Pre-FY Trading Update

1. Revenue Record retail volumes of ~65,000 in FY26, up 8.0% on FY25. No explicit revenue figure disclosed. FY1 consensus: £1,265.8m. Volume +8% is a strong leading indicator; revenue per unit likely broadly stable (metal margin performance was "record"). Implied revenue: if FY25 was ~60,185 units (65,000 / 1.08) at ~£19,500/unit = £1,173m (consistent with actual £1,173.1m), then FY26 at 65,000 units × ~£19,500/unit = ~£1,267m — essentially in-line with consensus £1,265.8m on volumes alone. However "record metal margin performance" could lift revenue/unit slightly.

"Record retail volumes of c.65,000 in FY26, up 8.0% on FY25"

2. EPS / Earnings PBT: "expected to be c.£7.5m, up 83% (FY25: £4.1m)." Consensus FY1 PBT: £7.4m. Beat: +£0.1m, +1.4% vs consensus — essentially in-line, very slight beat.

EBITDA: "c.£27.0m, up 13.0% (FY25: £23.9m)." Consensus FY1 EBITDA: £28.5m. This is a miss: −£1.5m, −5.3% vs consensus EBITDA. The PBT beats consensus but EBITDA misses — this implies higher depreciation/amortisation or IFRS16 lease costs than modelled, or a different adj/reported bridge.

FY26e EPS bridge (FY27):

  • FY26 base: PBT c.£7.5m → tax at ~25% → PAT ~£5.6m → diluted EPS ~7.0p (79.6m shares). FY1 consensus 6.7p → slight beat.
  • FY27 bridge:
    • (1) New base EPS: ~7.0p
    • (2) New Leeds store (summer 2026): incremental revenue c.£50–60m p.a. at maturity, PBT contribution c.£1.0–1.5m at ~2% PBT margin → EPS +1.2–1.9p at full run-rate (not until FY28)
    • (3) Organic volume growth: used car market growing 2.2%, MOTR growing 6% in calendar 2025. If sustained: ~4% organic volume growth → 67,600 units FY27 → revenue +£50m → PBT +£1m → EPS +1.2p
    • (4) Metal margin normalisation: "record" FY26 metal margin may partially normalise in FY27
    • (5) Leeds store pre-opening costs: ~£2–3m drag in FY27
    • Implied FY27 EPS: 8–9p — below FY2 consensus 10.5p. The 10.5p consensus may be too aggressive given Leeds is unlikely to fully contribute until FY28, and metal margins may normalise. Alternatively, additional store openings could be announced. Current FY2 consensus looks stretched.

3. Volume and market share Record retail volumes ~65,000 units FY26, +8.0% vs FY25. MOTR grew 6.0% in calendar year 2025 vs market +2.2% — "continued outperformance of the used car market."

Agentic AI tool for reactivating closed quotes: ~900 incremental vehicle sales attributed (1.4% of FY26 volumes). Supply normalising: "more bulk deals" and "more vehicles directly through Sell Your Car channel."

"Since launching our new agentic AI tool to reactivate historic closed quotes, c.900 incremental vehicle sales can be attributed to this channel."

4. Margin / profitability "Record metal margin performance" — metal margin is the gross profit per vehicle (selling price minus buying price). This is the key operational metric. Record metal margin + record volumes = strong FY26.

EBITDA £27.0m vs consensus £28.5m = miss on EBITDA. PBT £7.5m vs consensus £7.4m = marginal beat on PBT. The gap between EBITDA miss and PBT beat implies lower-than-expected D&A, interest, or IFRS16 lease charges vs broker models. Return on Capital Employed: c.70% — high, consistent with capital-light model.

"aided by record metal margin performance, which helped offset inflationary pressures"

Labour cost inflation explicitly flagged: "ongoing inflationary pressures, notably in labour costs."

5. Capital / new stores New store: Leeds, summer 2026. First new store announcement in this cycle. Leeds provides access to a "new, large market." No financial guidance on capex or earnings contribution.

6. Qualitative tone / FY27 outlook CEO: "Whilst the macroeconomic uncertainty in recent weeks leads to a degree of caution due to the risks of increased inflation and interest rates, our superior customer service, omnichannel business model and exciting growth plans mean we are well placed to take advantage of opportunities to further increase market share and build long term value for shareholders."

"Macroeconomic uncertainty… degree of caution due to risks of increased inflation and interest rates" — this is cautious language on the outlook. Not a downgrade, but a flag. No numeric FY27 guidance.

EPS quality check: PBT c.£7.5m; expected tax at ~25% → EPS ~7.0p reported. Sharescope FY1 consensus 6.7p (adj basis). No obvious tax distortions flagged in the RNS. ✅ Clean.

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification

FY26 delivery: PBT £7.5m (+83% YoY, +1.4% vs consensus) — in-line to marginal beat. FY27 forward language: "macroeconomic uncertainty… degree of caution due to the risks of increased inflation and interest rates." No numeric FY27 guidance.
